**Explanation:**
Lao verbs do not conjugate for tense. Temporal aspects are marked with pre-verbal or post-verbal particles: ໄດ້ (past/achieved), ແລ້ວ (already/completed), ກຳລັງ/ພວມ (progressive), ຢູ່ (continuous), ຈະ/ຊິ (future).

**Pattern / Formula:**
`Past: ໄດ້ + Verb (or Verb + ແລ້ວ) | Progressive: ກຳລັງ + Verb (+ ຢູ່) | Future: ຈະ/ຊິ + Verb`

**Examples:**
- Lao: ຂ້ອຍໄດ້ໄປວຽງຈັນ
 Pronunciation: Khoy dai pai Viengchan
 Breakdown: I + [past marker] + go + Vientiane
 English: I went to Vientiane.
- Lao: ຂ້ອຍກິນເຂົ້າແລ້ວ
 Pronunciation: Khoy kin khao laeo
 Breakdown: I + eat + rice + [completed marker]
 English: I already ate.
- Lao: ລາວກຳລັງຮຽນໜັງສືຢູ່
 Pronunciation: Lao kam lang hian nang sue yu
 Breakdown: He + [progressive] + study + book + [continuous]
 English: He is currently studying.
- Lao: ພວກເຮົາຈະໄປຕະຫຼາດມື້ອື່ນ
 Pronunciation: Phuok hao ja pai talat mue uen
 Breakdown: We + will + go + market + tomorrow
 English: We will go to the market tomorrow.

In Lao, the tone of a syllable is determined by 3 factors: (1) Consonant Class (High, Mid, Low), (2) Syllable type (Live vs Dead, Vowel length), and (3) Tone mark (ໄມ້ເອກ, ໄມ້ໂທ).

- Lao: ຂາ (High + Live + No mark)
 Pronunciation: Khaa
 Breakdown: High class + long vowel live syllable
 English: Tone: Rising tone
- Lao: ຄາ (Low + Live + No mark)
 Pronunciation: Khaa
 Breakdown: Low class + long vowel live syllable
 English: Tone: High/Mid tone
